title: The Instance Hierarchy (DataModel)
summary: Everything in Roblox is an Instance parented in one giant tree rooted at game (the DataModel). Services are children of game; your content lives in their subtrees. Paths through this tree are how code finds anything.

explanation.whatItIs: One tree to rule them all: game → services → your objects → their children. The Explorer window IS this tree; your code walks it with dots, FindFirstChild, and WaitForChild.
explanation.whyItExists: Parenting defines existence (unparented = gone), replication (which container), rendering (workspace), and lifetime (destroy cascades).
whenToUse: Choose containers deliberately: what lives where defines who sees it
Remember Parent defines membership — reparenting moves objects between worlds
whenNotToUse: Deeply long paths as your primary API — fragile; pass references or use tags
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
game (DataModel)
 ├─ Workspace          (the 3D world)
 ├─ Players            (the people)
 ├─ ReplicatedStorage  (shared, replicated)
 ├─ ServerStorage      (server-only)
 ├─ ServerScriptService (server code)
 ├─ StarterGui / StarterPlayer / StarterPack
 ├─ Lighting, SoundService, …
 └─ your stuff lives INSIDE these
```
tips: game is a global; game:GetService("X") is the robust accessor
script.Parent chains from inside a script: script.Parent is its container
Services like Players are also Instances with children (each Player!)
GetFullName() prints an object's full path for debugging
commonMistakes: Dot-pathing through possibly-missing objects — nil crashes; guard the hops
Moving gameplay objects between containers casually (replication changes!)
Confusing the Workspace service with 'everything that exists'

examples.title: Paths and guards
examples.code:
-- Direct (only when existence is guaranteed):
local lighting = game.Lighting

-- Guarded hops:
local map = workspace:FindFirstChild("Map")
local boss = map and map:FindFirstChild("Boss")
if boss then
    print("Boss found at", boss:GetFullName())
end

-- From inside a script:
local tool = script.Parent          -- if script sits in a Tool
print(tool:GetFullName())           -- e.g. "Workspace.Raani.Wand" (example)
